$comment: ROOM SHAPE CATALOGUE — the ONLY legal room footprints for dungeon generation.
Mark 2026-08-22: 'these are the only type rooms to build from so these rooms stop looking like crap'.
w x h are INTERIOR tiles. Walls are NOT part of the shape - they are derived globally (_sheathe),
so every room is sheathed by exactly one tile of wall and no room owns a private wall ring.
ORIENTATION IS SIGNIFICANT: 3x4 and 4x3 are DIFFERENT entries, because Mark listed both.
A generator may place a room ONLY by naming a key here; DungeonEmergency.validate() rejects any
footprint not in this list, so an ad-hoc rectangle cannot ship.
HALLWAYS are corridors: w = width in tiles, len = run length. They never carry a roomId.
HALLWAY LENGTH IS CAPPED AT 10. Mark 2026-09-05: 'halls max 10 (usually 4-5), rooms on the main hall'.
RETIRED 2026-09-07 on that rule: H1x12 H1x16 H2x12 H2x16 H3x12 H3x16. They were still catalogued as
legal, named, first-class entries two days after the rule that outlawed them, and Section0.js's three
wing spines were authored H1x16 straight out of this list - the map did exactly what the catalogue
told it it was allowed to do. Removed outright rather than flagged legacy: a 'legacy' entry still
answers RoomShapes.shapeOf() and still passes the MAP_CENSUS hallway check, so it retires the
documentation and not the loophole. Nothing else in the tree referenced them (grep, 2026-09-07:
Section0.js only). H1x10 / H2x10 / H3x10 are the ceiling and 4-6 is the intended everyday length.
